body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-09, third repair in one day.

`findings/INDEX.md` is generated from `findings/items/*.json`, but **nothing verifies the
two agree.** No test in `tests/autopilot/` reads it (the suites that mention `INDEX.md`
are about `notes/upstream-pr/`, a different file). So drift is invisible until someone
regenerates by hand and happens to diff.

Measured today, on main: **170 item files against 164 index rows**, summary reading
`160 open, 4 closed` where the ledger holds `165 open, 5 closed`. Fixed twice already
(#1473, #1493) and drifted again within hours.

The mechanism, and why counting rows does not catch it: per-finding rows are **additive**,
so two branches each adding a row merge cleanly and both survive. The summary count line
is **not** additive — it is written from whatever view the generator had, and the last
writer wins. A row-count check therefore passes while the count line is wrong. Only
regenerate-and-diff detects it.

Contributing causes, all benign individually:
- `scripts/findings.py add` writes the item but does not regenerate the index.
- A session that regenerates while another has an uncommitted item would publish a row
  for a file that is not committed, so the careful move is to NOT regenerate — which
  leaves the index stale (this is exactly what #1490 did, deliberately).
- Direct-to-main pushes of item JSON skip PR review entirely.

**Do not fix this by adding a naive gate to `test-autopilot.sh`.** That test suite runs
inside preflight step [5/5], and preflight aborts the tick BEFORE phase-7 — the only
actor that can edit the ledger. A gate over a file the autopilot itself writes, without a
repair upstream of the gate, is a self-locking wedge. That is F-66d002, which cost three
dead ticks this morning over a malformed `completed.log` line.

The shape that works is the one `repair-completed-log.sh` already uses: run the repair in
the deterministic floor BEFORE preflight, then let the gate assert. Concretely — have the
tick run `findings.py index` and commit the result if it differs, and only then add the
consistency assertion. Repair first, gate second, never gate alone.
title: findings/INDEX.md has no consistency gate, so it drifts silently and is repaired by hand each time
